stories.title: iNaturalist
stories.author: bookofjoe
stories.summary: iNaturalist is a global social network and nonprofit platform that enables citizens to record, share, and crowdsource identifications of biodiversity observations from the natural world. The key insight is that these individual findings are shared with scientific repositories like the Global Biodiversity Information Facility, transforming personal encounters with nature into valuable data for researchers and conservationists.

stories.title: Show HN: I built a frontpage for personal blogs
stories.author: ramkarthikk
stories.summary: Blogosphere is an aggregator for independent personal blogs designed to preserve the human-centric "indie web" in an era of social media and AI-generated content. [news.ycombinator.com](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47625952) It offers a minimal, Hacker News-style interface that avoids algorithmic feeds in favor of recent posts curated by category and manual user submissions. [blogosphere.app](https://blogosphere.app/)

stories.title: We replaced RAG with a virtual filesystem for our AI documentation assistant
stories.author: denssumesh
stories.summary: Mintlify replaced its traditional RAG pipeline with a virtual filesystem that allows AI agents to interact with documentation through standard file operations like `ls` and `cat`. This architectural shift enables "agentic retrieval," where the model uses semantic search as a tool to explore and retrieve granular context rather than relying on a pre-constructed context window. This approach significantly improved accuracy and reduced hallucinations by giving the assistant more control over how it discovers information within the source of truth.

stories.title: Go on Embedded Systems and WebAssembly
stories.author: uticus
stories.summary: TinyGo is an LLVM-based compiler designed to bring the Go programming language to resource-constrained environments like microcontrollers and WebAssembly. It enables developers to run Go code on over 100 different hardware boards and produce highly compact WASM binaries for web browsers and edge computing.

stories.title: Samsung Magician disk utility takes 18 steps and two reboots to uninstall
stories.author: chalmovsky
stories.summary: The article highlights the extreme difficulty of removing Samsung Magician from macOS, noting that the software lacks a standard uninstaller and its internal cleanup script fails due to system permission errors. To fully purge the utility, users must manually execute a complex series of terminal commands and perform two Recovery Mode reboots to clear protected kernel extensions. The author criticizes Samsung for creating "malware-like" software that requires 18 technical steps to uninstall from a modern Mac.

stories.title: The Technocracy Movement of the 1930s
stories.author: lazydogbrownfox
stories.summary: The Technocracy movement of the 1930s, led by Howard Scott, sought to replace democratic governance with an anti-democratic state ruled by technical experts and engineers to achieve maximum industrial efficiency. Driven by the failures of the Great Depression, the movement proposed unifying North America into a "Technate" managed through energy accounting rather than traditional currency.

stories.title: Understanding young news audiences at a time of rapid change
stories.author: giuliomagnifico
stories.summary: Young audiences (18–24) have transitioned from being "online-first" to "social-first," increasingly bypassing news websites to access information via short-form video platforms like TikTok and Instagram. This demographic prioritizes individual creators and generative AI tools over traditional news brands, often avoiding mainstream media because they find it too depressing, irrelevant, or difficult to follow.

stories.title: Show HN: TurboQuant for vector search – 2-4 bit compression
stories.author: justsomeguy1996
stories.summary: TurboQuant is an implementation of a Google Research (ICLR 2026) algorithm that compresses high-dimensional vectors to 2–4 bits without requiring a training step, enabling zero indexing time. The library utilizes Rust and SIMD acceleration to match FAISS query speeds on ARM hardware while reducing memory usage by approximately 8–16x.

stories.title: A School District Tried to Help Train Waymos to Stop for School Buses
stories.author: phlummox
stories.summary: Despite a collaborative effort in Austin to train self-driving cars to stop for school buses, a Waymo vehicle improperly passed a bus with its stop arms extended after a remote human assistant incorrectly signaled the system to proceed. The incident highlights critical gaps in autonomous learning and the risks of human-in-the-loop error, especially as six human drivers also failed to stop during the same event.

stories.title: Async Python Is Secretly Deterministic
stories.author: KraftyOne
stories.summary: While async Python allows for concurrent execution, it remains "secretly deterministic" because its underlying single-threaded event loop processes tasks in a predictable, consistent order based on their scheduling sequence. By leveraging this behavior, developers can create durable workflows that maintain a stable execution order, enabling reliable replay-based recovery even when running multiple steps concurrently via `asyncio.gather`.

stories.title: Show HN: An evidence-rated encyclopedia of peptides
stories.author: uelbably
stories.summary: This comprehensive database provides evidence-rated profiles for over 60 research peptides, categorizing them by scientific maturity from FDA-approved drugs to preclinical-only compounds. By tracing every claim to primary literature and evaluating suppliers against rigorous purity standards, the platform serves as a transparent alternative to anecdotal forum consensus and aggressive marketing copy.
